name: Jason "Manifest Destiny" Clark
caption: One half of the first RSPCW World Tag Team Championship finalists at the federation's debut supercard.

tenures.source: The federation's own 14 March 1994 live-draw roster call (entry #2) and MegaWrestleFest, 10 April 1994, both served on this wing.
tenures.note: His administrative sign-offs, a separate out-of-character capacity, are marked in place wherever they occur in served text; this persona's billing is not affected.

name: "The Executioner" Mark Engel
caption: A founding wrestler and, from October 1994, the federation's own Chief of Broadcasting and head booker, whose ring name persisted from the tag-title match at the debut supercard through the injury angle that renamed the top title.

tenures.source: The 14 March 1994 live-draw roster call (billed "Mark 'Samson' Engel"); MegaWrestleFest, 10 April 1994 (tag title match, American Dream Team); the federation's own 22 July 1994 statement on Joe Petrow's retirement (billed "'The Executioner' Mark Engel"), all served on this wing.
tenures.note: The gimmick is repackaged between April 1994 ("Samson", of the American Dream Team) and July 1994 ("The Executioner") -- an ordinary mid-run repackaging, not a distinct persona. From October 1994 the federation also bills the name as its own Chief of Broadcasting; the wrestler billing itself is unaffected.

identity.note: The registry's own decorated-aka guard reads this name as a normalized substring match against executioner-iwf. Recorded distinct, not merged: the only record this entity has is a placing in the RSPWF Top 200, which gives a ring name and a federation tag and nothing else — no dates, no roster, no URL, so three of the collision doctrine's own four signals are simply absent and the no-merge default holds. Every held-promotion roster the ranked names were checked against came back with zero overlap. Reopenable the moment either side gains a record the other can be checked against.

name: "Dr. Destruction" Don Martin
caption: The federation's first Television Champion, crowned at its debut supercard.

tenures.source: The federation's own 14 March 1994 live-draw roster call, billed "Don 'Dr. Destruction' Martin", and MegaWrestleFest of 10 April 1994 (the TV Championship match), both served on this wing; corroborated by the persona's own first-person in-character reply in the 1st TV Taping thread, which this wing does not serve.
tenures.note: Cuts his own post-match promo in first person elsewhere in the wing's own record, in the voice of the persona.

name: "The Sadistic Swissman" Daniel Amsler
caption: A prolific heel and Iron Man Tournament participant, leader of the in-fiction stable "the Fatal Four".

tenures.source: The federation's own 14 March 1994 live-draw roster call; MegaWrestleFest of 10 April 1994 (the Iron Man Tournament, two rounds); and an in-character reply of 7 April 1994 signed "Daniel Amsler / The Sadistic Swissman", all served on this wing.
tenures.note: Signs his own in-character promos beside the ring name the cards bill him under.

name: "The Heartbreak Kid" Joe Petrow
caption: The federation's first World Heavyweight Champion, whose kayfabe career-ending injury five months into the fed's run had the title renamed in his honor.

tenures.source: The 14 March 1994 live-draw roster call (billed "Joe 'The Comeback Kid' Petrow"); MegaWrestleFest, 10 April 1994 (Iron Man Tournament final, won the inaugural World Heavyweight Championship); the federation's own 22 July 1994 retirement/title-renaming statement, all served on this wing.
tenures.note: Announces his own retirement and cuts an earlier promo, "Heartbreak Kid Speaks Out", in the voice of the persona; a rival's own in-character tribute on this wing carries him too.

tenures.source: First attested on this promotion's own cards from 10 January 1997. Won and was immediately stripped of the Cruiserweight Championship on the same night, 10 May 1997, after the outgoing champion was ruled to have misrepresented his own weight class. Won the World Heavyweight Championship on 1 August 1998 and was still billed champion as of the promotion's own last surviving December 1998 billing. Also credited with a World Tag Team Championship reign as half of a two-man team in early-to-mid 1998, and received four honors at the promotion's own December 1997 year-end awards broadcast (Best Interviewee, Best Face, Most Missed Departed Athlete, and a shared Best Match award).
tenures.note: Same author-owned character as this record's own held rspcw-1994 persona; merged under one character id.

Billed "Sychosys" Joe Petrow (this record's own held aka); loses the Deschenes Cup first round to "Outlaw" J.W. Hardin. Falls chronologically between the held rspcw-1994 and iiwf tenures, five months before the iiwf tenure's own 1 August 1998 title win.

name: "Hot Stuff" Chris Taylor
caption: The reigning World Heavyweight Champion by mid-1994, who kept the belt through its renaming for the rival he took it from.

tenures.source: MegaWrestleFest of 10 April 1994 (the Iron Man Tournament, reached the final); the federation's own 22 July 1994 statement naming him "the current RSPCW World Heavyweight Champion"; and the persona's own in-character reply on that statement, all served on this wing.
tenures.note: PENDING COLLISION (not a with-id join): the main privacy ledger's own "Chris Taylor" row (real-name, scoped to promotions/rspwf/archive/community-hall-of-fame-) states the identical billed string "'Hot Stuff' Chris Taylor" is already a registered fictional character on the held RSPWF wing; no characters.json id was found there to reference formally. Flagged in this wing's own registry provenance_notes and digest; not merged.

name: "Wild Will" Comer
caption: A debuting challenger who talked his way into a title shot and, by his own account, briefly held a tag championship.

tenures.source: MegaWrestleFest of 10 April 1994 (a post-match challenge, narrated) and "RSPCW Why it is here" of 10 October 1994, both served on this wing; corroborated by the persona's own in-character debut and title posts elsewhere in the held record, which this wing does not serve.
tenures.note: Issues an in-character debut challenge and a later tag-title complaint under the ring name the cards bill him under, elsewhere in the wing's own record.
